NDT training in Savannah: how it works for Savannah employers and technicians

NDT training for Savannah is delivered by Atlantis NDT as ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, either live online or onsite at your facility in Chatham, Effingham or Bryan County, under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification is issued by your employer under its written practice once you complete classroom hours, documented on-the-job experience, general, specific and practical exams, and a vision test.

That short answer hides a practical point that trips up many people searching for NDT courses in coastal Georgia. Under SNT-TC-1A nobody, not a school, not a training company and not ASNT itself, hands you a portable Level II card at the end of a class. The training course is one input. The employer that uses your inspection results is the body that certifies you, and it does so against its own written practice. So the first question for a Savannah technician is not "where is the nearest classroom?" but "which employer, or which prospective employer, will certify me, and what does its written practice ask for?"

Atlantis NDT does not run a physical training centre in Savannah or anywhere else. What we do is deliver the formal classroom portion of SNT-TC-1A training live online, so a technician in Pooler, Port Wentworth, Richmond Hill or Rincon can attend from home or from the site office, and deliver the hands-on and practical portions onsite at the employer's own facility, on the employer's own equipment and specimens. For a hangar-floor penetrant line, a port crane maintenance shop or a supplier welding battery-tray structures, that is usually a better fit than a generic classroom, because the practical work matches the parts your people actually sign off.

People who contact us from the Savannah area usually fall into one of four groups. First, working Level I and Level II technicians who want to add a method, for example a PT Level II on aerospace details who now needs ET for fastener-hole inspection, or an MT Level II on structural steel who needs UT to handle full-penetration welds. Second, fabrication and maintenance employers who have a crew doing inspection informally and now need it formalised because a customer audit, a Nadcap-driven supplier requirement or a new contract has asked for certified personnel. Third, career changers, often welders, machinists, aircraft maintenance technicians or veterans leaving Hunter Army Airfield or Fort Stewart, who want a clear route into inspection. Fourth, experienced Level IIs preparing for the ASNT Level III examinations. Each of those groups needs a different starting point, and the sections below are written to help each one find it.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Savannah

Every method below is available for Savannah employers and technicians at Level I and Level II, with Level III examination preparation available for experienced candidates. The table maps each method to the kind of Savannah-area work it is typically used for. It is context, not a promise of employment: which methods a given employer needs is set by its customers, its codes and its written practice.

MethodLevelsWhat Savannah employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic testing (UT)I, II, III prepThickness surveys on paper-mill and LNG-terminal piping, weld examination on crane and structural steel, bond and laminate checks in aerospace supply workNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
Phased array UT (PAUT)II, III prepWeld examination where radiography is impractical, including port structures, pressure equipment and heavier fabricationConventional UT Level II recommended before PAUT
Time-of-flight diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepSizing of planar flaws in thick-section welds on vessels and heavy fabrications serviced from the Savannah areaConventional UT Level II recommended
Radiographic testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipe and vessel welds, castings, and film or digital interpretation for fabrication shops and power-plant outage contractorsNone for Level I; radiation-safety certification is a separate regulatory requirement
Magnetic particle testing (MT)I, II, III prepCrane, container-handling and structural welds, lifting gear, forgings and automotive-supplier steel componentsNone for Level I
Liquid penetrant testing (PT)I, II, III prepNon-ferrous aerospace parts, stainless piping, machined components and weld surface examinationNone for Level I
Visual testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld visual inspection on fabrication and construction work, in-service inspection, and as the base for every other methodNone for Level I
Eddy current testing (ET)I, II, III prepFastener holes, surface cracks in aluminium structure, conductivity checks, and heat-exchanger tubing at industrial plantsNone for Level I; strong PT or MT background helps

Which method first in Savannah? For someone entering the field with no certifications, the three surface methods, VT, PT and MT, are the most common starting points because they are required across almost every local sector, from aerospace detail parts to port lifting equipment. UT is the method that most often moves a technician from general inspection work into higher-responsibility roles, because it is used for volumetric weld examination, corrosion mapping and thickness surveys. ET is particularly relevant in a city whose largest manufacturing employer builds aircraft, since eddy current is a mainstay of aluminium-structure and fastener-hole inspection. PAUT and TOFD are best approached after conventional UT, because the advanced techniques assume you already understand sound-beam behaviour, calibration and flaw characterisation.

Each method course covers the physics of the method, equipment and consumables, calibration and technique selection, the interpretation of indications, how acceptance criteria from codes and specifications are applied, and how results are recorded and reported. Level II courses go further into setting up techniques from a written procedure, evaluating indications against acceptance standards and supervising Level I personnel. Level III preparation concentrates on the Basic examination (materials, processes, other methods and SNT-TC-1A itself) and the method examinations, including writing and reviewing procedures. See the method pages on our NDT training overview and the dedicated ASNT Level III training page for more detail.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Savannah, step by step

The steps below are the same framework any SNT-TC-1A employer uses. What changes from company to company is the detail written into each employer's written practice. The recommended minimum training and experience hours by method and level are summarised in our NDT training requirements matrix; your employer's written practice may require more.

  1. Confirm the employer's written practice. Before you enrol, find out which document will govern your certification. A Gulfstream supplier, a port contractor and a paper-mill maintenance contractor may each have different written practices and different customer overlays. If your company does not yet have one, that is the first gap to close.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Attend the method-specific training for the level you are seeking. With Atlantis this can be live online for the theory, with practical sessions onsite. Keep the training records: course outline, hours, dates and instructor.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. SNT-TC-1A expects documented experience in the method under the supervision of certified personnel. Record it as it happens, with dates, methods, techniques and hours, and have it verified. Experience that was never written down is very hard to prove at audit time.
  4. Pass the general examination. A written test on the principles of the method, set and graded under the authority of a Level III.
  5. Pass the specific examination. A written test on the equipment, procedures, codes and acceptance criteria you will actually use in your employer's work.
  6. Pass the practical examination. A hands-on test on real specimens, where you demonstrate that you can set up the technique, detect and evaluate indications and report the result correctly. This is administered by a Level III or a designee under the written practice.
  7. Pass the vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation checks as required by the written practice, with near vision repeated at least annually.
  8. Receive employer certification. The employer certifies you in writing for the method and level, based on the combined results. The certification is valid with that employer.
  9. Maintain and recertify. Keep vision tests current, maintain continuity in the method, and recertify at the interval your written practice sets. If you change employers, the new employer must certify you under its own written practice, though it may accept your prior training and experience records.

Our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide explains each step in more depth, including what auditors look for in personnel files.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Savannah crews

The delivery model is straightforward, and we prefer to say it plainly. Theory is taught live online by an instructor in real time, so trainees can ask questions, work through examples and be assessed, rather than clicking through pre-recorded slides. Practical training and practical examinations take place onsite at your facility in the Savannah area, using your equipment, your reference standards and specimens that resemble the parts and welds your crew inspects. Everything is run under ASNT Level III oversight. For individuals without an employer, the online theory route is open, and we will be honest about how the practical and experience portions can be arranged, because those cannot be completed remotely under any recognised scheme. Read more on our online NDT training page.

Scheduling matters in Savannah because the local work runs on very different calendars. Aerospace production and completions lines run to delivery schedules. Port maintenance is planned around vessel calls and crane availability. Pulp and paper mills and regional power stations run planned maintenance outages, often in the spring and autumn shoulder seasons, when inspection crews are stretched. A sensible plan is to put the classroom portion into quieter weeks, run live-online sessions in shorter blocks so a crew does not lose whole shifts, and schedule the onsite practical so that trainees are qualified before the next outage or shutdown rather than in the middle of it. Tell us your constraints and we will propose a timetable; cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

For multi-site or growing employers, we also run structured corporate NDT training programmes that combine method courses, written-practice work and Level III examination services into one plan. Ask about onsite training for your Savannah crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Savannah

Savannah's inspection market is unusually mixed for a city of its size. That mix is good news for technicians, because it means several different sectors compete for people who hold the same core certifications, and it is a planning challenge for employers, because the codes and customer requirements differ widely from one sector to the next.

Aerospace manufacturing and completions. Business-jet manufacture and service around Savannah/Hilton Head International Airport, together with the machine shops, composite shops and finishing suppliers that feed it, generate demand for PT, ET, UT and VT. Aerospace primes and their suppliers typically layer customer specifications, and often NAS 410 or EN 4179 and Nadcap accreditation, on top of general qualification requirements. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based; we do not offer NAS 410 certification, so aerospace employers should treat our method training as one component of their own qualification scheme and check their prime's requirements.

Automotive and battery manufacturing. The Hyundai Metaplant America site in Ellabell, Bryan County, and the supplier plants that have grown along the I-16 and I-95 corridors bring welded steel and aluminium structures, stamping dies and production tooling. Structural welding here is commonly done to AWS standards such as D1.1 or D8.1, which puts VT, MT, PT and UT to work, and suppliers often need a written practice and a Level III relationship for the first time.

Port, cranes and logistics. The Georgia Ports Authority's Garden City Terminal and Ocean Terminal, and the distribution and heavy-equipment businesses around them, rely on MT and UT of crane structures, spreaders, lifting gear and structural welds, with VT throughout. Much of this work is done by maintenance contractors whose inspection function has grown gradually and now needs formal certification to satisfy clients and insurers.

Energy, LNG and process industry. The LNG facility on Elba Island, fuel terminals along the Savannah River, and process plants in the port area use ASME B31.3 process piping, pressure vessels built to ASME Section VIII, and low-temperature storage, all of which call for UT thickness and weld examination, RT, PT on stainless and VT. Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh in Effingham County and the Plant Vogtle nuclear site upriver near Waynesboro draw outage and maintenance contractors from the Savannah labour pool; nuclear work carries its own additional quality-assurance and qualification requirements.

Pulp and paper. Large paper and packaging mills in the Savannah area run recovery boilers, digesters, tanks and extensive piping. Boiler work is typically done to ASME Section I and the National Board Inspection Code for repairs, with UT thickness surveys, MT and PT a routine part of every outage.

Military and public infrastructure. Hunter Army Airfield and Fort Stewart generate aviation and ground-equipment maintenance work, and bridges such as the Talmadge Memorial Bridge fall under Georgia Department of Transportation inspection programmes, where steel-bridge welding and inspection follow AWS D1.5.

Radiography licensing in Georgia. Georgia is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography with sealed gamma sources is licensed by the state's Radioactive Materials Program within the Georgia Environmental Protection Division, under rules equivalent to federal 10 CFR Part 34. Radiographers and radiographer's assistants must meet state training and certification requirements, typically including a radiographer certification such as ASNT's Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel (IRRSP) programme, before working unsupervised with a source. X-ray equipment registration is handled separately at state level, so confirm the current agency for your equipment. Crews that cross the river into South Carolina work under that state's own agreement-state programme. Our RT course covers the NDT method and film or digital interpretation; it does not replace the radiation-safety training and certification your licence requires. Employers should build both into the same plan.

What local employers typically ask for when hiring or promoting: a current employer certification at Level II in the relevant method, documented experience hours that can be verified, a clean vision record, and, for aerospace and nuclear work, evidence that you can work to a customer specification rather than just a general code. Salary questions come up often; rather than quote numbers we cannot verify for Savannah, we point people to our NDT salary guide, which explains how level, method and sector drive pay.

Level III services and written practices for Savannah NDT companies

Many Savannah-area companies that perform inspection are not inspection companies. They are fabricators, maintenance contractors, machine shops and manufacturers that have grown an inspection function because their customers require it. The most common problem we see in that situation is not a lack of training; it is the lack of a governing document and a Level III to run the programme. Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer is responsible for its written practice, for designating who administers examinations and for keeping personnel records that will survive an audit.

Atlantis supports employers in three ways. First, written-practice development: we draft or revise a written practice that fits your methods, levels, customer overlays and organisation, and that reflects how your work is actually done. Second, Level III services: examination preparation and administration, procedure writing and review, technique sheets, and periodic review of personnel files and certifications. Third, training plans that tie these together, so that the classroom hours, experience logs and examinations are all recorded in a way your auditor, customer or insurer will accept. The SNT-TC-1A guidance page explains the employer's obligations in more detail.

For a supplier preparing for its first customer audit, the practical sequence is usually: write or update the written practice, confirm which personnel need which methods and levels, gap-analyse training and experience records, then train and examine. Doing it in that order avoids training people to a scheme that later has to change. Book a Level III consultation for your Savannah company.

Practise before the practical exam

The practical examination is where many candidates lose confidence, especially those who have learned the theory well but have had limited hands-on time. Atlantis trainees can use the Practical NDT 3D simulator to practise 12 NDT methods across five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Savannah technicians that range is useful because the local work spans the hangar, the fabrication shop and the process plant.

The simulator is a practice tool. It helps trainees rehearse set-up sequences, scanning patterns and indication recognition before they touch a real specimen, and it is a convenient way to revise between shifts. It does not replace the practical examination, which must be performed on real specimens under your written practice, and it does not count as documented on-the-job experience. For written-exam revision, try our UT Level 2 practice questions and the related mock-exam articles on the blog.

Your instructor

Atlantis NDT training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, examination preparation and the Level III aspects of each programme, including written-practice and procedure work for employers. Savannah trainees work with the same instructional team and materials used across all Atlantis programmes, delivered live online and onsite at the employer's facility.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Savannah

How do I get NDT certified in Savannah?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. You complete formal training in the method, build documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer then certifies you in writing under its written practice. Atlantis provides the training, examination preparation and, for employers, the Level III and written-practice support.

Can I take NDT training online in Georgia?

Yes. The classroom (theory) portion of Atlantis training is delivered live online, so technicians anywhere in Georgia can attend. Practical training and the practical examination must be done hands-on with real equipment and specimens, which we deliver onsite at the employer's facility. Online theory alone does not make you certified.

Is there an Atlantis NDT school or training centre in Savannah?

No. Atlantis does not operate a physical training centre in Savannah. Training is delivered live online and onsite at your company's facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. For employers, onsite delivery usually means practical work on the exact parts and welds your crew inspects.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the written practice you are certified under and on what you already hold. SNT-TC-1A sets recommended minimum classroom hours and experience hours for Level I and Level II, and the experience requirement usually takes longer to meet than the classroom portion. See the training requirements matrix for the recommended figures, and check whether your employer requires more.

Do I need a license for industrial radiography in Georgia?

Radiography companies using radioactive sources need a licence from Georgia's Radioactive Materials Program, because Georgia is an NRC Agreement State. Individual radiographers must meet the state's training and certification requirements for radiation safety, commonly including a radiographer certification such as ASNT IRRSP. NDT method certification in RT is a separate requirement handled under your employer's written practice.

What does NDT training cost in Savannah?

We do not publish prices. Cost depends on the method, level, number of trainees, whether the practical is delivered onsite, and whether Level III examination services or written-practice work are included. Send us your requirements and we return cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Request a Savannah training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Savannah employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used personnel-qualification framework in US industry, and Savannah-area fabrication, maintenance, process and many aerospace employers work within it. Remember that SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based: a new employer recertifies you under its own written practice, though it may credit your prior training and experience. Aerospace primes may also require NAS 410 or EN 4179, which Atlantis does not offer.

Which NDT method should I start with in Savannah?

For most newcomers, VT, PT and MT are the practical first steps because they are used in almost every local sector. UT opens up weld examination and thickness-survey work, and ET is valuable for aerospace structure. The best answer is the method your current or target employer needs, so ask them before you enrol.

Can our company train and certify its own inspectors?

Yes. That is exactly how SNT-TC-1A works. You need a written practice, access to a Level III who can administer or oversee examinations, and training and experience records for each person. Atlantis can provide the written practice, the training and the Level III services as a package.

Can you train our crew around a plant outage or production schedule?

Yes. Live-online theory can be split into shorter sessions, and onsite practical days can be scheduled before a planned outage or between production runs. Tell us your windows and we will propose a plan.

Do you offer ASNT Level III exam preparation for Savannah candidates?

Yes. Level III preparation covers the Basic examination and method examinations, delivered live online. See the ASNT Level III training page for the structure.

Do you offer API, CWI or NAS 410 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Some Savannah employers also ask for API inspector certifications, AWS CWI or NAS 410 qualification, and those are obtained through their own bodies and schemes. Our method training can complement them, but it does not replace them.
